quotes.text: A. Description of Exterior Old City Hall appears as a three story plus mansard French Second Empire building with a central pavillion projecting from the School Street, or main elevation. The pavillion is three bays across and one bay deep, rises an additional story above the mansard level and is topped by a tall "dome" - actually a square convex mansard with dormers and an elaborate curbing. Rectangular in plan, the building is nine bays across the main elevation and six bays along its sides. Each elevation is of dressed granite. The fenestration pattern is regular with tall round headed windows on the principle floors and segmental arches on the third floor.

note: Seeded 5 Sep 2026, WP-11.3 Tranche 2, the mid-nineteenth-century city house cluster. The canonical American Second Empire public building, and the survey states the pavilion system as a bay count rather than as an adjective: nine bays with a three-bay centre one bay deep, rising one storey above the mansard. That is the second-empire node's 'pavilion system that the cottage styles had abandoned', in a number a checker could hold a facade against. The survey also says the third-floor windows are segmental where the principal floors are round-headed, which is storey diminution expressed in the window head and not in the height.
